finding.claim: When an address contains characters outside [0-9a-f:/%], parse() builds AddressError.parseMessage by wrapping each bad character in a span but never HTML-escapes the input. address-error.ts:9-10 documents parseMessage as HTML-escaped and safe to insert as-is, so this breaks that contract. The leading-zero branch at ipv6.ts:763 does escape its prefix, so this one is inconsistent with it. Only characters in the bad-character set are wrapped. Raw `<`, `>`, `"`, `'` and `&` therefore reach parseMessage unescaped. I could not build a working script-injection payload for plain text insertion. Any tag name containing a letter g-z is split by the wrapping spans, and every `<` is immediately followed by ``. Insertion into an attribute value is different: a raw `"` is not neutralised there, so this is a live injection if a consumer follows the documented advice and places parseMessage in an attribute. Severity is low to medium and depends on how the consumer renders it.
finding.source: Any string passed to `new Address6(str)` or `Address6.isValid`, `fromURL`, etc. from untrusted input, e.g. `x" onmouseover="alert(1)` or `<a href=...>`.
finding.sink: AddressError.parseMessage (an HTML fragment) that consumers are told to render as markup (address-error.ts:4-12).

finding.guards_checked: The RE_BAD_CHARACTERS check only detects bad characters; it does not escape them. helpers.escapeHtml exists (src/v6/helpers.ts:1) and is used at ipv6.ts:763 and in link(), but not here. The `/` and zone-suffix strips at ipv6.ts:137-153 do not sanitize the remainder. No other caller escapes the message. The RE_BAD_ADDRESS branch at ipv6.ts:815-818 is only reached after the bad-character check passes, so it is safe.
